tap-tempo.assumptionNote: Tempo is measured from your taps only - it assumes you tap steadily on the beat. A pause longer than 2.5 seconds resets the measurement, and the metronome click is a simple synthesized tick, not a studio click track.
benefits: Find the exact tempo of any song in seconds - just tap along.
Spacebar tapping works too, so you can tap without looking at the screen.
Built-in metronome plays your tapped tempo back for practice.
Milliseconds-per-beat readout helps you set delays and DAW tempos precisely.

faqs.a: BPM (beats per minute) counts how many beats fit in one minute. 60 BPM is one beat per second, 120 BPM is two beats per second. Most pop songs sit between 90 and 130 BPM; ballads are slower, dance tracks faster.

Tap on the beat - usually where you would clap or nod your head. Tap at least 4-6 times; more taps give a steadier average. The tool uses your last 8 intervals, so early wobbly taps stop affecting the result.
Tap the big button with your finger, or press the spacebar - both work. On desktop, the spacebar is easiest because you can keep your eyes on the music. Each press counts as one beat.
faqs.q: Can I tap with the keyboard?

faqs.a: Yes - toggle the metronome on and it clicks at your tapped tempo, with a flashing display on each beat. It is perfect for checking whether a tempo feels right before you commit to it.
60,000 divided by the BPM: at 120 BPM each beat lasts 500 ms. Producers use this to set delay times - a quarter-note delay at 120 BPM is 500 ms, an eighth note is 250 ms.
faqs.q: How do I convert BPM to milliseconds?

faqs.a: No - and that is normal. Human tapping varies by a few BPM even for steady tappers. The tool averages your last 8 taps to smooth this out. If the number jumps wildly, slow down and tap more deliberately on the strongest beats.
faqs.q: Why does my BPM keep changing slightly?

tap-tempo.formula:
BPM = 60,000 / average tap interval (ms)
Milliseconds per beat = 60,000 / BPM
Example: taps every 500 ms: BPM = 60,000 / 500 = 120.
howTo: Tap the big button (or press the spacebar) in time with the music - on every beat.
Tap at least 4 times; 8 or more taps give the steadiest reading.
Read your BPM. Toggle the metronome to hear it played back.

tap-tempo.quickAnswer: Tap the big button (or the spacebar) on every beat - after 4 taps you get a live BPM reading that steadies as you keep tapping. Four taps 500 ms apart measure exactly 120 BPM, since BPM = 60,000 / average interval. tap-tempo.workedExample:
Finding a song's tempo:
1. The song plays. You tap on each kick-drum hit: tap... tap... tap... tap...
2. Your tap times: 0, 512, 1005, 1518 ms. Intervals: 512, 493, 513 ms.
3. Average interval = (512 + 493 + 513) / 3 = 506 ms.
4. BPM = 60,000 / 506 = 118.6 BPM.
5. Keep tapping: after 8 taps the reading settles at 118.8 BPM.
6. ms per beat = 60,000 / 118.8 = 505 ms - set your delay to 505 ms for quarter notes.
